references.text: Moses tells the elders to wait while he goes up the mountain, which mirrors Abraham's words to his servants to wait while he and Isaac go further to worship.
The book of Hebrews explains that Abraham believed God could raise Isaac from the dead, shedding light on Abraham's trusting words 'we will come back to you' in Genesis 22:5.
Jesus tells the disciples to sit and wait while He goes further to pray in Gethsemane, a structural parallel to Abraham's instructions to his servants to wait while he and Isaac go further.
Abraham's answer to Isaac that God Himself will provide the lamb expands on the trusting faith behind his words in verse 5 about 'we will come back'.
Paul describes Abraham's faith in God who gives life to the dead, illuminating Abraham's conviction in Genesis 22:5 that both he and the boy would return.
Contrast between Abraham's faith in returning with his son (22:5) and his protection ensuring the son does not return to the old land (24:6).
The direct narrative connection where Abraham's 'Here I am' in 22:11 confirms his willingness to 'worship' as expressed in 22:5.
